$comment: Fake deployment scenario of the fault-recording acceptance
(tests/integration/fault_recording_test.py). One runtime, no application,
no hardware.
The machine reports healthy, connected joints long enough for the runtime to
start and for a DDS peer to discover the state writer. Then joint 0
disconnects and stays disconnected: the first latched fault. While that
fault is still latched, joint 1 disconnects too, so the recorder must add a
second occurrence with another joint while the published report keeps the
first one. Both reconnect, but the runtime stays in Fault until a Reset.
Finally joint 0 disconnects again, after the condition had recovered,
so the tracker reports it as a new occurrence. Both reconnect afterwards so
the harness can reset the latch into a healthy ZeroTorque and stop the
runtime cleanly; a reset with the condition still present would latch it
again on the next tick.
`connected: false` with `valid: true` establishes exactly one condition per
joint (JointDisconnected); a false `valid` would add JointFeedbackInvalid
observations for the same joint and make the assertion ambiguous.
elapsed_us is monotonic from process start and mandatory; an entry applies
from its time onwards. imu.valid is true so the recorded rows carry the IMU
snapshot the configuration collects even though imu_required stays false.
